column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses an active plural verb for burning human bones; BSB expresses their burning passively.
The Hebrew leaves the giver of the sign unnamed; BSB supplies “the man of God.”
The Hebrew names “the king” and later “Jeroboam” and explicitly says he stretched his hand from the altar; BSB combines the names and rearranges the location.
The Hebrew repeats “the altar” as the source of the poured ashes; BSB leaves that second occurrence implicit.
The Hebrew twice names the LORD’s “face” in the entreaty and separately asks for prayer “on my behalf”; BSB leaves the face image and the separate beneficiary implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “half your house”; BSB interprets this as “half your possessions.”
The Hebrew uses an active verb, “he commanded me”; BSB uses passive “I was commanded.”
The Hebrew leaves the traveler unnamed; BSB supplies “the man of God.”
The Hebrew first says “his son” with singular verbs and later “they told their father”; BSB uses plural sons and verbs throughout.
The Hebrew says the sons saw the way; BSB says that they showed it to him.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed; BSB supplies “the prophet.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves both speaker and addressee unnamed; BSB supplies “the prophet” and “the man of God.”
The Hebrew separately says he cannot return with him and come with him; BSB leaves the coming phrase implicit.
The Hebrew uses an active verb, “he spoke to me”; BSB uses passive “I have been told.”
The Hebrew leaves both the first speaker and the liar unnamed; BSB supplies “the prophet” and “the old prophet.”
The Hebrew leaves the returning man unnamed and connects with “and”; BSB supplies “the man of God” and begins “but.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses “the mouth of the LORD” for what was defied; BSB uses “the word of the LORD.” It leaves the crying speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies “the prophet.”
The Hebrew repeats the prohibitions about bread and water; BSB condenses them as “not to do so.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately says the donkey stood beside the body and the lion stood beside the corpse; BSB combines their standing into one phrase.
The Hebrew repeats “the corpse”; BSB uses “it” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew says “the mouth of the LORD”; BSB uses “the command of the LORD.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed; BSB supplies “the old prophet.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew first calls him “the prophet” and later names “the city of the old prophet”; BSB begins “the old prophet” and later uses “his own city.”
Close to the Hebrew.
